rules.subject: data_hall
rules.rationale: People enter a data hall only through a mantrap, a two-door vestibule where one door must close before the other opens, so entry is checked one person at a time.
exceptions: Freight entries to the hall, which are controlled by other means

rules.subject: mantrap
rules.rationale: The mantrap is the last of layered controls: the secure entry and its desk come first, then the mantrap, then the hall. Which of the entry and the desk the mantrap hangs off varies between proposals.
exceptions: Small sites with the desk and the entry in one room

rules.subject: office
rules.rationale: Offices and the visitor lobby sit on the public side of the mantrap, so people who do not work on the equipment have no route to the data hall.
exceptions: Operators who need a desk with a view of the hall

rules.subject: electrical_room
rules.rationale: Switchgear, UPS and battery rooms are rooms of their own, fire-rated, next to the halls they feed, which shortens busway runs and keeps maintenance out of the hall. Whether this is adjacent or separate is a matter of wording in the proposals, see the conflict ledger.
exceptions: Modular designs that put power inside the unit

rules.subject: mechanical_room
rules.rationale: Cooling air handlers sit immediately beside the hall they serve, so duct and pipe runs are short and airflow is predictable. Chillers and other wet plant are a separate matter, see the next rule.
exceptions: Rooftop or yard cooling plant reached by risers

rules.subject: heavy_plant
rules.rationale: Generators and chillers are noisy, heavy and wet, so they are in a yard or plant room apart from the hall, with fuel storage apart from the generators.
exceptions: Containerised plant placed against the building

rules.subject: cooling_room
rules.rationale: Cooling and electrical plant do not share a room, so each can be maintained independently and water stays away from switchgear.

rules.subject: electrical_path_a
rules.rationale: The A and B electrical feeds run in physically separate rooms and routes, so one fire, flood or error cannot take both out and the hall keeps redundant power.
exceptions: Facilities that do not claim path diversity

rules.subject: mechanical_room_a
rules.rationale: Cooling is redundant too: two independent mechanical rooms and routes serve each hall, so the loss of one leaves the hall cooled.
exceptions: Facilities without a cooling redundancy requirement

rules.subject: loading_dock
rules.rationale: Equipment arrives at a dock that opens onto a service corridor leading toward the hall, and not through the offices or the entry.

rules.subject: staging_room
rules.rationale: New equipment is unpacked and tested in a staging room by the dock, before it is carried into the data hall, so cardboard and dust stay out of the hall.

rules.subject: network_operations_center
rules.rationale: Operators work in a room with comfort heating and cooling and not among the racks. Where it sits relative to the hall and the entry is contested, see the conflict ledger.
exceptions: A single desk inside a small hall

rules.subject: security_room
rules.rationale: Whoever watches the cameras and the doors sits beside the mantrap and the main entry, so they see who is going in and can respond.

rules.subject: meet_me_room
rules.rationale: Where carriers connect (the meet-me room) and the network distribution sit at the edge of the hall, so the network runs into the hall are short.

conflicts.topic: Electrical room next to the hall, or separate from it

positions.position: Adjacent to the hall, for short runs (confidence 0.9).
Immediately adjacent, to limit cable runs and voltage drop (confidence 0.9).
Separate from the hall as the predicate says, but its rationale puts the rooms next to the halls and not inside them (confidence 0.75).

conflicts.resolution: Adjacent, and a room of its own: the literal predicates differ and the rationales do not. The rule uses adjacent_to; the separate-room point is in its rationale.

conflicts.topic: Cooling plant beside the hall, or apart from it

positions.position: Mechanical rooms adjacent to the hall, on at least two sides.
The hall is not directly accessible from the mechanical room, to limit leaks; contested, as liquid cooling puts water in the hall (confidence 0.4).
The chiller room is separated from the hall.

conflicts.resolution: Split by plant: air handlers are adjacent, and chillers and generators are apart. The wet-plant-door point of the sonnet proposal is not adopted, for its low confidence and its own caveat.

positions.position: A separate room, usually with glass onto the hall floor (confidence 0.7).
In the secured area, in view of the entry control, outside the hall (confidence 0.45).
The monitoring center near the main entry (confidence 0.9).

conflicts.resolution: Only that it is not inside the hall is adopted. Whether it faces the hall or the entry is left open, and the monitoring role is a separate rule.
